newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bazy hopes for 10 pct ROE for UAP France.
newsitem.headline: Bazy hopes for 10 pct ROE for UAP France.

text.p: UAP France, Union des Assurances de Paris ' main profit-making centre, is aiming for a return on equity of around 10 percent this year and 15 percent within three or four years, UAP France chairman Dominique Bazy said.
"I think as of this year our return on equity should not be far from 10 percent," he told Reuters in an interview.
"UAP France should achieve in the next three or four years a return on equity of at least 15 percent, " he added. That compares with a return on equity of below five percent in 1995.
Bazy, who has headed UAP France since August, expects a fall in the division's life insurance activities for the full year after they shrank 0.8 percent in the first half.

For UAP as a whole, Bazy, often touted as a potential successor to group chairman Jacques Friedmann, said the group should achieve a return on equity of 10 percent "fairly quickly", adding he hoped it would be "a little bit before" the turn of the century.

UAP posted a 2.07 billion franc loss for 1995. The loss reflected 4.5 billion francs of provisions. The downturn extended to UAP France whose contribution to group profit fell to 587 million francs from 1.72 billion. Of that, life insurance contributed 292 million francs, down from 466 million.
UAP France's turnover last year accounted for 40 percent of group sales.
Bazy said he was pessimistic about the outlook for UAP Vie in 1996. "For us, it will not be very easy this year. The second half is not looking very good," he said.
Bazy said he was aiming to give policy holders of life insurance contracts a return this year of about six percent, which would be below the rest of the market, expected to be around 6.5 percent.

UAP Vie has been hit by weak asset returns. But asset allocation has been tilted now more toward bonds from stocks. Bonds now make up 65 percent of UAP Vie's investment portfolio compared with 59 percent at the end of December.
Bazy said this move should help returns. He said the average return from UAP Vie assets was equivalent to the return on seven year borrowings, "just slightly under six percent".
He also said more work had to be done to improve returns from property holdings which make up 15 percent of UAP Vie's assets.
The group sold last June a portfolio of troubled property loans with a gross value of 3.2 billion francs for one billion francs net to a U.S. fund specialising in distressed debt.
UAP still has a portfolio of troubled loans worth a net 1.4 billion francs. "We've no intention of disposing of them. We're capable of managing them just as well as any American fund," Bazy said.
